content.user_title: Choose the Right Agent or Skill
content.value_statement: Choosing between agents and skills can slow AI-assisted work. This skill maps task types to the right Claude, Codex, or Claude Code tool.
actual_capabilities: Maps common tasks to lightweight skills or heavyweight agents.
Provides quick references for coding, DevOps, data, and content tools.
Explains when to use the Skill tool or Task tool.
Links to detailed catalogs for agents and skills.
Limits recommendations to a small set of relevant tools.
limitations: Does not install, execute, or configure the recommended tools.
Catalog accuracy depends on the included reference files.
Some recommendations assume named skills or agents are available.
Web scraping guidance may require policy and legal review.

use_cases.title: Route Development Tasks
use_cases.description: Find the right skill for language, framework, database, or DevOps questions before starting implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Assistant Workflows
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for when a team should use a skill, agent, or general task prompt.

use_cases.title: Review Tool Choices
use_cases.description: Check whether a requested AI workflow uses the narrowest useful tool for the task.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Tool for a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to recommend the best skill or agent for this task: [task]. Explain the choice in one paragraph.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to compare [skill or agent A] and [skill or agent B] for [task]. Recommend one option.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Tool Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to plan which skills and agents should handle each step of this workflow: [workflow]. Keep the list short.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Routing Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to review this proposed tool-routing plan: [plan]. Identify overuse, missing skills, and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: I need help finding files named config and then explaining a React hook.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use file-search for locating files, then react-ops for the hook explanation. No agent is needed unless analysis becomes broad.

output_examples.input: I need to optimize a PostgreSQL query and prepare a pull request.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use postgres-ops for query analysis, then git-ops for commit and pull request workflow guidance.

output_examples.input: I need a plan for migrating a Node project to modern modules.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use javascript-ops first. Use Plan only if the migration requires architectural tradeoffs across many packages.

best_practices: Start with a skill for lookup, syntax, or reference tasks.
Use an agent when the task needs judgment, planning, or optimization.
Confirm the recommended tool exists in the current environment before invoking it.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch multiple agents for simple reference lookups.
Do not treat catalog suggestions as permission to bypass site restrictions.
Do not assume unavailable skills can be loaded without installation or confirmation.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you need to choose a Claude, Codex, or Claude Code skill or agent for a task.

faq.question: Does it run the recommended tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides routing guidance and reference catalogs only.

faq.question: Can it recommend more than one tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It should keep recommendations to the smallest useful set.

faq.question: Does it replace domain-specific skills?
faq.answer: No. It helps select those skills, then the selected skill provides domain guidance.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No. The core guidance comes from local skill and agent catalog files.

faq.question: Is web scraping guidance always safe?
faq.answer: No. Users must follow site terms, laws, and authorization requirements.
